title: October 6, 1949: Nehru laid the foundation stone for a military academy unlike any other in the world.

sources.text: The Week - Khadakwasla: The cradle of India's military leadership

caption:
October 6, 1949: Nehru laid the foundation stone for a military academy unlike any other in the world.

The academy was designed as the world's first tri-service military academy - training Army, Navy and Air Force cadets together from day one, instead of separately. The original paperwork called it the 'National War Academy'; Nehru objected to the name at the ceremony itself and had it changed to 'National Defence Academy.'

The NDA was formally commissioned on December 7, 1954 and inaugurated on January 16, 1955 - becoming the training ground for generations of India's military leadership, built around a tri-service model many countries still don't use.

Nehru's small edit to the academy's name - from 'war' to 'defence' - still frames how India's military has trained its officers for over 75 years.
